analysis: Examined three changes. (1) ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.swift: discoveryMode now keeps `auto` MTP for coordinator-paired setups only when the build declares a public assistant (`declared`). discoveryArguments and requireDiscoveredQuote take an optional `declared` policy. When a declaration exists, requireDiscoveredQuote (lines 113-116) requires the native helper's quoted policy to equal the declaration exactly. The target-only path still goes through requireAssistant(nil). Artifact, config and request-scope checks are unchanged (lines 99-108), and the manifest and artifact-SHA binding in automaticCandidate is unchanged. This only widens which assistant is offered for coordinator traffic, through a build-declared allowlist (ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant, not supplied). The speculative-decoding parity-qualification claim in the removed comment is not re-verified here. The declaration's contents and qualification evidence are outside the supplied evidence. (2) EngineV2Bridge+MTP.swift line 72-76: mtpStatusSnapshot returns a pair snapshot for DistributedCBv2Engine when MTP is configured. This is telemetry and status only, built from DistributedCBv2Engine.mtpTotalsSnapshot (not supplied), and it feeds heartbeat and status fields with no auth effect. The hard-coded placementDecodesWithHead: true is a self-reported posture. (3) ProviderLoop+ClusterPairSlot.swift lines 196-202: configureMTPStatus is set to active when ready.tensorAssistant is non-nil. This is self-reported local posture (T-056 class, not a serving authorization). configureMTPStatus starts a sampler Task, which retirement cleans up through bridge shutdown (assumed, not shown). I found no new trust-boundary crossings, key handling, or plaintext exposure. Open questions for integration: whether the coordinator treats mtp_enabled/mtp_active as routing or authorization evidence (T-056/T-053), and whether ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant is gated on parity qualification.
